title: As the Sweet Flower That Scents the Morn
description: As the Sweet Flower That Scents the Morn in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 582 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Death of an Infant”, where the book credits them to the Epis. Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: As the sweet flower that scents the morn, But with-ers in the ris-ing day, Thus love-ly was this in-fant's dawn, Thus swift-ly fled its life a-way.

lines: As the sweet flower that scents the morn,
But withers in the rising day,
Thus lovely was this infant's dawn,
Thus swiftly fled its life away.
It died ere its expanding soul
Had ever burnt with wrong desires,
Had ever spurned at Heaven's control,
Or ever quenched its sacred fires.
Yet the sad hour that took the boy
Perhaps has spared a heavier doom, —
Snatched him from scenes of guilty joy,
Or from the pangs of ills to come.
He died to sin; he died to care;
But for a moment felt the rod;
Then, rising on the viewless air,
Spread his light wings, and soared to God.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
